description:
FILED s451z, measured while closing #711.  PRE-EXISTING; #711 (the OPEN => 0
half) is CLOSED and this is what is behind it.

REPRO:

    use File::Temp qw(tempfile);
    my ($fh, $f) = tempfile();          # OPEN defaults to 1
    print "got $f\n";

        perl  got /tmp/XXXXXXXXXX-ish name, $fh open
        PCL   Undefined subroutine &File::Temp::sysopen called

`sysopen` is a perl BUILTIN.  It is not in `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` and not in
`Pl/PExpr/Config.pm`'s `known_no_of_params` (the only mention is inside a
comment listing builtins at Config.pm:519), so the bareword lowers to an
ordinary sub call in the module's own package and dies at run time.

MEASURED with #711 in (s451z probe p711f): rows 1-4 (`tempfile(OPEN => 0)` in
all four spellings -- bare, with a leading TEMPLATE, with DIR, with SUFFIX)
now agree with perl exactly; row 5, `tempfile()`, is this task.

SCOPE: `sysopen FILEHANDLE, FILENAME, MODE, PERMS` -- the O_* flag constants
come from Fcntl, which File::Temp already imports and PCL already transpiles.
The natural landing is beside `p-open` in the runtime, with `Pl/PExpr/Config.pm`
giving it a [3,4] arity and the bareword-filehandle branch the `open` family
already has.

BAR: the repro plus `tempfile()` with a TEMPLATE, `sysopen` onto a bareword
handle and onto a `my $fh`, the O_CREAT|O_EXCL failure mode (perl returns
false and sets $!), and the PERMS argument; then RESTORE the `tempfile()`
spelling in `Pl/t/stdio-buffering-01.t` row 7, whose comment points here (it
builds its scratch path from $$ instead).


DONE s452aa (Opus agent AA, round 11).

RUNTIME (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, beside p-open as the task's landing said):
  %p-sysopen-direction (flags)  -- the CL direction from O_ACCMODE (logand 3):
      0 :input, 1 :output, 2 :io, and 3 DIES naming the value (rule 12: a value
      the caller then consumes).
  %p-sysopen-impl (fh path flags &optional perms)
      * PERMS defaults to perl's 0666; the umask applies in either case because
        open(2) applies it.
      * BUFFERING comes from %p-output-buffering -- #542's ONE reading of
        perl's policy -- asked DIRECTLY rather than through
        %p-line-buffer-if-tty, because that helper exists to REBUILD a stream
        CL `open` already made with the wrong buffering, and here the fd-stream
        is ours to build right the first time.
      * failure: sb-posix:syscall-error -> *p-stored-errno* from the syscall's
        own errno (the established shape in this file), return false.
      * success: %p-install-fh (so every handle shape open supports works) and
        return 1, which is what perl returns.
  p-sysopen macro -> (%p-sysopen-impl (%p-fh-arg fh) â¦), so a bareword handle
      is auto-quoted exactly as p-open does it.  Exported.

EMISSION (three one-line changes, all keyed on the mechanism):
  Pl/PExpr/Config.pm   known_no_of_params: sysopen => [3,4]
  Pl/ExprToCL.pm       %RUNTIME_NAMES gains `sysopen` (so it emits (p-sysopen â¦)
                       rather than a pl- user call)
  Pl/PExpr.pm          the bareword-filehandle PRE-REGISTRATION is SHARED with
                       `open` (same first-argument slot) instead of copied.

PROBES: 12 shapes vs perl 5.40.3, ALL identical -- O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC with
explicit 0600 PERMS (write, read back, mode bits); a BAREWORD handle with
O_RDONLY; O_APPEND (does not truncate); O_CREAT|O_EXCL on an existing file
(false + errno 17) and a missing directory (false + errno 2); O_RDWR round-trip
through one handle with seek; the 3-arg default PERMS under umask 0022 (0644);
O_TRUNC; the return value being exactly 1; syswrite through the handle;
File::Temp tempfile() bare AND with a TEMPLATE + DIR.

GUARDS: Pl/t/fileio-02.t 34 -> 40 rows (six sysopen rows, each compared against
perl by the file's own test_io, so the O_* numbers and the errno come from perl,
not from the test).  Pl/t/stdio-buffering-01.t row 4 is BACK on the `tempfile()`
spelling its comment had been pointing at this task for, and the comment now
records that the pointer is discharged.

GENERATION: v2-400 (an emission-affecting change).  All three checked-in
artifacts regenerated -- their BODIES came back BYTE-IDENTICAL, only the gen=
stamps moved, which is the expected result for a change that adds a NEW name.
pack.t re-run after the rebuild: 5636/89 = the blessed baseline exactly.

A/B: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 files + 6 shapes; emission-ab over the 23
lib shims SAME=23 DIFF=0 RCDIFF=0.  Population scan for the widening: the only
`sysopen` users are perl-tests/lfs.t (in the sweep's known-hang skip set) and
op/lfs.t, op/taint.t, op/cproto.t, op/coreamp.t in the companion -- all four
measured, ALL SAME as their snapshot rows (lfs.t 0/0 DIFF, taint.t TRANSPILE,
cproto.t 71/183, coreamp.t XDIFF).

RESIDUE FILED: #740 -- the first version of the O_TRUNC probe read `-s $f` and
disagreed with perl, which turned out to be #403's family, not sysopen: `-s` on
an existing EMPTY file is a defined 0 in perl and undef in PCL.  The probe was
rewritten to read stat()[7]; sysopen itself was identical on all 12 shapes.
subject: `sysopen` is not implemented -- File::Temp::tempfile() (the DEFAULT, OPEN => 1) dies "Undefined subroutine &File::Temp::sysopen called"
